requirement: `habeas status` and the mdBook requirements index MUST generate their Definition/Evidence Markdown tables through the same renderer. That renderer MUST calculate column widths, align the columns, and display the same evidence-state labels in both outputs. Callers MAY select different definitions and supply different kind-labeled name cells so mdBook can link to detail pages.
rationale:
I found no gaps. Both outputs build their table through one renderer, and tests cover each output.

**Same renderer.**
- `src/commands.rs#fn[status_markdown_with_options]` is marked {impl}. It delegates to `status_markdown_with_github`, which builds `rows` of (name cell, `evidence.state().label()`) and calls `render_evidence_table(&rows)`.
- `src/index.rs#impl[DetailPlan]/fn[populate]` is marked {impl}. It builds `rows` of (linked name cell, `evidence.state().label()`) and calls the same `render_evidence_table(&rows)`.
- `render_evidence_table` is in `src/markdown.rs`, and both modules import it from there.

**Column widths and alignment.**
- `src/markdown.rs#fn[render_evidence_table]` computes each column's width as the maximum cell length, with the header text as a minimum.
- It pads every cell of the header, separator and data rows to that width using `{:<width$}`.
- The `status_table_alignment` requirement marks it, so the width and alignment code is reachable from both callers.

**Same evidence-state labels.** Both callers take the label from `EvidenceState::label()` via `evidence.state().label()`. The renderer takes the label as a string and passes it through unchanged.

**Callers MAY select different definitions and supply different name cells.**
- Status filters definitions by glob, `--all` and state, and uses plain `` `name` (kind) `` cells.
- The index uses every detail-page definition and supplies cells linked to the detail pages, as `[`name`](href) (kind)`.
- The renderer accepts both, so this MAY clause is supported.

**Tests.**
- `tests/commands.rs#fn[status_tables_align_each_column_to_its_widest_cell]` is marked {test}. It runs `habeas status` and `habeas status --all`. It asserts that the pipes align, that each column is as wide as its widest cell, and that the labels are Valid, Missing, Determination false and Invalid.
- `src/index.rs#mod[tests]/fn[index_shows_evidence_states_and_links_generated_chapters]` is marked {test}. It asserts the same pipe alignment and column widths in the mdBook index table. It also asserts the same state labels and the linked name cells.
